source.title: Understanding Visual Feature Reliance through the Lens of Complexity
source.authors: Thomas Fel; Louis Béthune; Andrew Kyle Lampinen; Thomas Serre; Katherine L. Hermann

record.tranche_reason: The paper invokes superposition to motivate extracting more features than neurons, but does not test the toy-model superposition claim or any listed version. Its own feature-encoding measurements do not establish overlapping, nearly orthogonal feature directions or capacity-driven polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The paper says its overcomplete dictionary is intended to avoid the superposition or feature-collapse problem, and cites Toy Models of Superposition. The dictionary size and classification accuracy are not results testing the claim. The feature-encoding and redundancy results below are included as related findings; none tests a listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper uses an overcomplete NMF dictionary (10,000 features over 2048 channels) on ResNet50, motivated by superposition and citing Toy Models. Its results concern feature complexity, flow, learning time and importance. The Hoyer-score analysis of dictionary atoms is in a vision CNN, not an LLM, and does not measure superposition geometry, capacity competition or SAE feature canonicity. No listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the appendix encoding results. The main conclusions are about the complexity metric itself. They introduce a V-information-based complexity metric and find a spectrum of simple-to-complex features. Simple features are carried by residual connections, while complex ones are built with the main branches. Complex features are learned later in training. Simplicity bias strengthens over training, and important features simplify over time (a 'sedimentation' process). None of these conclusions concerns superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an ImageNet-trained ResNet50 and an overcomplete NMF-based concept dictionary to study feature complexity and encoding; it does not reproduce the toy-network method or measurements in Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that feature-encoding strategies may vary across architectures, but does not test that variation here.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet50, NMF dictionary atoms range from near-one-hot (Hoyer near 1) to distributed across neurons, with no clear relation to complexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an ImageNet CNN, overcomplete dictionary features vary from neuron-aligned to distributed, independent of feature complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: More complex features are less redundant under masking-based CKA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an ImageNet CNN, more complex dictionary features are encoded less redundantly across neurons.

record.problems: The main study focuses on one architecture, ResNet50. The paper notes limitations of its complexity measure and that other dictionary-learning methods may yield different feature properties. The relevant feature-encoding and redundancy results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry analysis.
No test of importance versus dedicated or shared dimensions. The importance analysis concerns logit contribution versus complexity, not capacity allocation.
Does not examine causes of polysemantic neurons.
No LLM is studied. The vision-CNN finding that dictionary atoms range from local to distributed is related but out of scope.
The NMF dictionary is used as given. Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested; the limitations section notes other methods may give different features.
Features are assumed to be 1-D directions. No multidimensional comparison is made.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition appears only as motivation for using more dictionary features than neurons. 'Avoid this problem of superposition' is the authors' framing, not a tested result. The study is peer-reviewed (NeurIPS 2024) and covers a single architecture.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse features exceeding dimensionality, overlapping or nearly orthogonal geometry, or sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Does not test whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Studies a vision model, not LLMs; it does not test the stated LLM feature-spreading or SAE-recovery claim.
Uses dictionary-extracted features but does not test whether they are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hoyer scores of 10,000 dictionary feature vectors to assess local versus distributed encoding.
rows.measure: Hoyer score, interpreted as local encoding near 1 and distributed encoding near 0
rows.note: The text reports substantial variation: some features have scores near 1, while others are more distributed. This does not measure superposition geometry or test a listed version.
rows.check: Hoyer scores of NMF dictionary atoms describe how localised each atom is across neurons in a vision CNN. This does not measure any version's effect, so 'observed' has no version to be observed against. It is figure-only, with no numbers.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature complexity with distributed encoding.
rows.measure: Relationship between complexity and degree of distributed encoding
rows.value: figure only; text reports no clear relationship
rows.note: The paper reports that complexity does not appear to determine whether a feature is localized to one neuron or distributed across several.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature redundancy by comparing CKA with original activations and activations masked at multiple levels.
rows.measure: Redundancy score based on CKA under progressive masking, compared with feature complexity
rows.value: figure only; text reports complex features tend to be less redundant
rows.note: The text describes the association qualitatively; it does not report numerical values in the text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
